minutes.headline: Committee approved all line-item transfers, a grant-funded co-teaching coach posting, and a custodial negotiator; equity audit Q&A had no action.
minutes.summary: The committee heard public comment opposing mandatory SEL and the equity audit, approved three bundles of line-item transfers, accepted a concession stand donation, and approved posting a grant-funded co-teaching coach. It also appointed a member to negotiate with the custodians and food service workers, heard an athletics report, answered equity audit questions with no action taken, and discussed bullying and capital planning.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved all three bundles of line-item transfers as presented, including money to repair storm-damaged equipment.
The committee approved posting a grant-funded co-teaching coach position.
The committee appointed one member to negotiate with the custodial and food service workers; a first ground-rules meeting may fall in April vacation week.
The committee took questions on the equity audit and took no action; no recommendations were accepted.
The committee accepted a memorial-fund donation for concession stand upgrades and waived or completed readings on several policies.

why_it_matters: Contract talks with custodians and food service workers now have a named committee negotiator, and the outcome will shape future school operating budgets and the tax bill that funds them.
The equity audit was left with no recommendations adopted, so any program or spending that follows would need a later vote residents could attend or comment on.
watch_next: Next week's meeting is to take up capital plan items, including the school plow sander and track and field.
The superintendent is to check whether the school attorney can give a bullying presentation sooner, possibly at a separate meeting.
